title: Switching doors wins the car twice as often
body: Your first pick hides the car with probability 1/3. The host, who knows, opens a goat door, concentrating the other 2/3 onto the single remaining closed door. Switching therefore wins two thirds of the time. The host's informed choice, not the doors themselves, moves the probability.
source_hint: Monty Hall problem (vos Savant, 1990; formal analyses)
